title: R_4(5(x-y)=2z) = 625
statement: The 4-colour Rado number of 5(x-y) = 2z is exactly 625 = 5^4: every 4-colouring of {1,...,625} contains a monochromatic solution, and some 4-colouring of {1,...,624} avoids one. The cell (a,b) = (5,2) is BLANK in Table 10 of Chang-De Loera-Wesley (ISSAC 2022), the only published four-colour table for this family, so this is a new exact four-colour Rado number. It confirms the a^k pattern at a point where a >= b+2 and gcd(a,b) = 1 hold and nothing was known.

checked_by: axeyum in-tree backward DRAT checker (axeyum_cnf::check_drat_backward, ADR-0382, pure Rust) on s4, via the new `akb2_frontier check` mode: parse 60.546 s, check 8703.254 s, 103,409,097 steps re-derived. The check ran on a DIFFERENT HOST from the solve: parsing plus backward checking needed ~56 GiB resident for the 8.82 GB certificate (a 6.6x blow-up measured twice this session), which did not fit the 61 GiB solving host. The formula was regenerated on the checking host from (a,b,k,n)=(5,2,4,625) by the same encoder, so nothing about the instance's identity travelled with the file.

prior_art.citation: Y. Chang, J. A. De Loera, W. J. Wesley, 'Rado Numbers and SAT Computations', ISSAC 2022 / arXiv:2210.03262
prior_art.establishes: NEW. Table 10 of arXiv:2210.03262 is the only published four-colour table for this family: 20 cells, 13 populated (12 exact plus the bare '> 225' at (2,3)), 7 blank. (5,2) is one of the blanks. Census read from the rendered v1 PDF cell by cell and cross-checked against this repository's ledger over all 25 k=3 cells and all 12 exact k=4 cells with zero disagreements, so the blank is a real blank and not a transcription slip. OEIS full-text search for 'Rado number' returns 7 sequences, none for this family at k >= 3 colours.

evidence.supports: identifies F_625, the formula the refutation is about
evidence.notes: 2500 variables, 255748 clauses. Re-checked by regeneration from (a,b,k,n)=(5,2,4,625) with the encoder written independently of the generator of record, not by hash alone.

NOT SEARCHED FOR. This is Chang-De Loera-Wesley's Lemma 4.1 colouring written down from the construction: point j takes colour v_5(j) + 1, the 5-adic valuation, which on [624] takes exactly the 4 values 0..3. Emitted and checked in under 0.02 s by `cargo run --release -p axeyum-search --example akb2_frontier -- valuation 5 2 4 624 witness.txt`. Verified four independent ways: the encoder's own first_monochromatic, the family's brute-force first_violation, CnfFormula::evaluate on the one-hot assignment, and this ledger's own Python enumerator. NOTE: this colouring is byte-identical to the one in rado-r4-a5-b1 (same sha256). That is correct, not a copy-paste error: the valuation colouring c(j) = v_5(j)+1 does not depend on b, so the same object witnesses the lower bound for every b coprime to 5.

regeneration.command: cargo run --release -p axeyum-search --example akb2_frontier -- solve 5 2 4 625 F_625.drat witness-625.txt 10
regeneration.note: The certificate is 8,819,268,223 bytes of text DRAT and is NOT distributed. Producing it took 6576 s; checking it took 8763.8 s and ~56 GiB resident, so a verifier should budget roughly 7x the file size in RAM and more wall clock than the solve. This instance is the measurement behind that rule: it is why `akb2_frontier check` exists, since the proof had to move from the host that produced it to one that could afford to check it.

evidence.checker_command: cargo run --release -p axeyum-search --example akb2_frontier -- solve 5 2 4 625 F_625.drat witness-625.txt 10
evidence.notes: Produced on s1 and checked on s4, deliberately. The proof was streamed to disk by TextProofSink; the producing process was then killed before its in-process check could be OOM-killed at 55.7 GiB of 61, the complete certificate rsynced to a 123 GiB host, and re-derived there by check_drat_backward after axeyum's own parse_drat read it back. The certificate was never at risk: the sink flushes before the driver reads the file, and the stored bytes end in the empty clause. 103,409,097 steps, parse 60.546 s, check 8703.254 s.

notes: Both sides of the threshold, each by a different mechanism: the lower bound is a construction written down and checked, the upper bound is a machine proof re-derived by an independent checker. Neither side used an external solver.
